amendments.rule: **A purpose `לְ` + infinitive construct recast as a finite clause gives the complementizer to the preposition and the supplied subject and modal to the infinitive.** The ASV writes *that men may bring*, *that I may be glorified*. This is rule 48's division outside the privative `מִן`, and for the same reason: the complementizer is what the preposition contributes, while a supplied subject pronoun and a separately written modal belong to the verb, as rule 17 keeps a subject pronoun with its verb. The corpus puts the *that* on the preposition in 28 units across 17 chapters and never on the infinitive, so this too is settled. Where the ASV writes no complementizer at all there is nothing to place, and the `לְ` goes `unrepresented` under rule 40. **A temporal preposition before an infinitive construct is read the same way.** Where `בְּ` or `כְּ` + infinitive is recast as a finite temporal clause — `בְּחֻמָּם` → *When they are heated*, `בְּלֶכְתּוֹ` → *when he went*, `כְּבֹאֲךָ` → *When thou comest*, `כְּכַלֹּתְךָ` → *when thou hast made an end* — the preposition takes the *when*, the infinitive keeps the verb, and the suffix takes the subject pronoun the ASV writes for it under rule 18. The corpus aligns `בְּ` to *when* in 45 units, so the temporal case is settled on the same footing as the purpose case. Read the preposition that is present rather than its lemma: a `לְ` heading such a phrase goes the same way even where its object is the noun rather than the infinitive, as in `לְקוֹל תִּתּוֹ` → *When he uttereth his voice*. **But only a preposition can take it.** Where none is present and the construct relation itself is what the English *when* realizes, rule 19 puts that word on the *nomen rectum*, which is the infinitive: `עֵת הִדְרִיכָהּ` → *at the time when it is trodden* gives *at the time* to `עֵת` and *when ... is trodden* to the infinitive.
amendments.why: JER.51 applied rule 52's division five times (51.16, 51.39, 51.59, 51.61, 51.63) to a temporal `בְּ`/`כְּ` + infinitive, a case the rule's text does not name — it speaks only of a purpose `לְ`. Each pass had to reason by analogy to a rule about *that*, and the analogy is what the contract should state. The corpus agrees decisively: LEMMA=בְּ aligns to *when* in 45 units, headed on the preposition, and never puts the *when* on the infinitive. The closing rider is added because the same chapter meets the case at 51.33, where `עֵת הִדְרִיכָהּ` has no preposition and the *when* goes to the rectum under rule 19; without it a later pass reading the widened rule could reach for a preposition that is not there. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule so that rule 52's own sentence about the purpose `לְ` is not left standing as if it were the whole of the division.

conventions: The WLC and the ASV divide 51:21/22 differently: the chariot clause of WLC 51.21b (wə-nippaṣtî bəkā rekeb wə-rōkəbô) is printed by the ASV at the head of 51:22. Rule 10 forbids reaching into a neighbouring verse, so the eight source tokens s009-s016 are each unrepresented in 51.21 and the fifteen English tokens t001-t015 are one added unit with a null target head in 51.22. Nothing is missing from either verse; do not re-align one against the other, and read the eleven BSB disagreements clustered in 51.21 as this offset rather than as candidates.

Where an article morpheme stands in a phrase for which the ASV writes a possessive or another determiner instead of *the* — ba-mməṣādôt → *in their strongholds* (51.30), ba-ššānāh → *one year* and *another year* (51.46), ka-ttannîn → *like a monster* (51.34) — the article is unrepresented under rule 29, since rule 15 makes the article's English *the* and nothing else, and the supplied *their*, *one*, *another* or *a* joins the noun's own unit and is never added.

hāyāh + lə is not uniform in this chapter, and the difference is the ASV's rather than the Hebrew's: the preposition is unrepresented under rule 21 at 51.37 (*shall become heaps*), 51.41 (*is become a desolation*) and 51.43 (*are become a desolation*), but at 51.30 the ASV writes *are become as women* and the lə takes that *as*. Read what the ASV spends on the preposition before reaching for rule 21.
mē-ʾên → *without* is one fused unit headed on the negation, at 51.29 and 51.37 alike (rules 30, 50).

report: One real cross-verse split: bāḥûr → *young men* / *the young man*. At 51.22 the unit heads on *young* (rule 31's lexeme-bearer) and at 51.3 it heads on *men*. Every other adjective-plus-supplied-generic-noun unit in the chapter heads on the modifier — gibbôr → *mighty men* (51.30, 51.56, 51.57), ḥākām → *wise men* (51.57), zāqēn → *the old man* (51.22), kəpîr → *young lions* (51.38), qādôš → *the Holy One* (51.5) — so 51.3 is the lone outlier and is patched to head on *young*. Nothing else in that verse changes.

Candidates checked and cleared as ASV-licensed rather than split: yōšəbêy → *them that dwell* (51.1) against *the inhabitants* (51.12, 24, 35); nepeš plus suffix split at 51.6 but fused at 51.14 and 51.45, which is rule 30's one-English-word condition working in both directions; every article marked unrepresented, each because the ASV writes no *the* for that phrase; every ʾēt (H853) unrepresented except the appositional *even* at 51.60, which rule 16 names; the eight nāpaṣ → *break in pieces* units, uniform in edge and head; rule 49's copula-on-the-preposition, applied without exception at 51.11, 17, 19, 25, 33, 35, 48 and 64.

hāyāh + lə looks like a split and is not: the preposition is unrepresented at 51.37, 51.41 and 51.43, where the ASV writes nothing for it, and aligned to *as* at 51.30, where the ASV writes *are become as women*. Rule 21's clause is conditioned on the recasting leaving no English word, so the difference is the target's. Recorded as a convention so a later reader does not re-open it.

The WLC/ASV verse-division offset at 51:21/22 is the chapter's one structural oddity, and the two verses dispose of it symmetrically: eight source tokens unrepresented in 51.21, fifteen target tokens in one added unit with a null head in 51.22. Given rule 10 that is the only ledger-legal option, and I have not disturbed it. It accounts for eleven of the fifteen individually listed BSB disagreements.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error. The two ʾet rows are rule 16, the eleven R rows are rule 21 and rule 40 recastings (spare/show/escaped with a bare object, the resultative lə, the possessive lî of 51.20), and the fourteen Td rows are rule 29 phrases for which the ASV writes no *the*. All are the documented convention differences the report itself predicts. No accepted edge was changed to improve the rate.

One amendment, to rule 52: the chapter applied rule 52's division to a temporal bə/kə plus infinitive construct five times (51.16, 39, 59, 61, 63) for a case the rule's text does not name, and the corpus aligns bə to *when* in 45 units. The amendment also forestalls the no-preposition case, 51.33's ʿēt hidrîkāh, where rule 19 puts the *when* on the rectum. No new rule was written for the verse-boundary offset: rule 54 shows the pipeline resolving verse-level edition differences before the packet is built, so a boundary offset belongs there and not in the contract.
